commands.short: Server for casas-eternas — stores worlds and derived artifacts.
commands.long:
Server for casas-eternas.

It stores what the browser client makes and derives: named worlds, and the
content-addressed artifacts baked from them. It generates nothing itself.

One binary runs every part; "start --target" chooses which. Configuration
comes from casas.yaml, CASAS_* variables and flags — one vocabulary: the
config key is the flag name is the variable name.

flags.name: config
flags.usage: Path to the configuration file. Default: ./casas.yaml if it exists. Flags and CASAS_* variables override the file.

flags.name: global.admin.socket
flags.usage: Path of a unix socket serving this process's admin API (user administration, over plain HTTP). Whoever can reach the socket is admin — file permissions gate it, no login. Empty serves none.

flags.name: global.listen
flags.usage: Address to listen on, as host:port. ":8080" binds every interface, "127.0.0.1:8080" keeps a local instance off the network.

flags.name: global.tls.ca
flags.usage: Path to the CA that CLIENT certificates are verified against. Setting it turns on mutual TLS.

flags.name: global.tls.cert
flags.usage: Path to the server certificate. Enables HTTPS together with global.tls.key.

flags.name: global.tls.key
flags.usage: Path to the server private key. Enables HTTPS together with global.tls.cert.

commands.short: Administers the auth subsystem of a running server.
commands.long:
Administers the auth subsystem of a RUNNING server, over its unix
admin socket (global.admin.socket). Whoever can reach the socket is admin —
file permissions gate it, no login. In a split deployment these commands
answer only in the process running the auth target.

commands.short: Manages global roles — what a user's sessions may claim.
Binds a user's global role; admin sessions carry the adm claim from their next login on.
commands.example:
casas-eternas auth role bind ada admin
  casas-eternas auth role bind ada user     # back to the default

commands.short: Lists every binding that deviates from the default role.
Creates a user: identity and password in one step.
commands.example:
casas-eternas auth user add ada
  echo -n 'the-password' | casas-eternas auth user add ada --password-stdin

flags.name: password-stdin
flags.usage: Read the password from stdin instead of prompting — for scripts and Jobs. Trailing newlines are stripped; nothing else is.

commands.short: Removes a user. Their worlds fall to admins; re-adding the name mints a NEW identity.
Lists every user, and whether they can log in.

commands.example:
casas-eternas auth user passwd ada
  echo -n 'the-password' | casas-eternas auth user passwd ada --password-stdin

flags.name: password-stdin
flags.usage: Read the password from stdin instead of prompting — for scripts and Jobs. Trailing newlines are stripped; nothing else is.

commands.long: Starts the selected modules in a single process.
commands.example:
casas-eternas start --target all           everything, for local play
  casas-eternas start -t world -t artifacts  storage only, no client
  casas-eternas start -t client              frontend only

flags.name: artifacts.cap
flags.usage: Size the artifact store may grow to before least-recently-used artifacts are evicted, e.g. "50GB". 0 or empty keeps it unlimited.

flags.name: artifacts.storage.dir.path
flags.usage: The directory of the artifact store.

flags.name: auth.storage.dir.path
flags.usage: The directory the auth subsystem's state lives in — auth.db, holding users and their credentials. A users.json left by an older server is imported once when the database is founded.

flags.name: client.storage.dir.path
flags.usage: The directory the built client is served from. Empty serves only /config.json, which is what a dev run alongside "npm run dev" wants.

flags.name: docs.storage.dir.path
flags.usage: The directory the built documentation site is served from (npm run build:docs). Empty serves nothing, which is what a dev run wants.

flags.name: global.auth.mode
flags.usage: How the server establishes who is asking: none, password, oidc — none is local (one synthetic owner), password means this server holds the users, oidc a foreign provider. See docs/decisions/server-auth.md.

flags.name: global.auth.session-key
flags.usage: Path to the key that session tokens are signed with, at least 32 bytes. Without it a key is generated at startup, which means sessions do not survive a restart and several replicas do not agree.

flags.name: global.auth.session-ttl
flags.usage: How long a login lasts before a password is needed again. Has no effect until token renewal exists; until then global.auth.token-ttl is the one that matters.

flags.name: global.auth.token-ttl
flags.usage: How long an issued token is valid.

flags.name: global.services.artifacts
flags.usage: URL of the service running the artifacts module, when it is not co-resident. Empty expects it in this process.

flags.name: global.services.relay
flags.usage: NATS URL of the relay (the message bus), when it is not co-resident, e.g. nats://relay:4222. Empty expects it in this process.

flags.name: global.services.worlds
flags.usage: URL of the service running the world module, when it is not co-resident. Empty expects it in this process.

flags.name: jobs.max-concurrent
flags.usage: How many jobs may run at once. One level-1 job of a real world holds some gigabytes, so raising this raises the memory the host must have.

flags.name: jobs.worker
flags.usage: Path to the job worker bundle (npm run build:worker). Defaults to job-worker.mjs beside the binary.

flags.name: relay.listen
flags.usage: Address the relay accepts worker connections on, as host:port. The default keeps it on this machine: there are no worker credentials yet.

flags.name: relay.storage.dir.path
flags.usage: The directory of the relay's message store (JetStream).

flags.name: target
flags.usage: The target modules to start: all, client, world, artifacts, jobs, docs, auth, relay. Repeatable. Deliberately NOT a config-file key — the same file serves differently-targeted processes.

flags.name: world.keep-revisions
flags.usage: How many revisions of each world to retain; older ones are pruned on upload. 0 keeps every revision.

flags.name: world.storage.dir.path
flags.usage: The directory the saved worlds live in.

commands.short: Prints the build, the API version and the bake pipeline this binary carries.
commands.long:
Prints what this binary is.

The pipeline version is the one worth reading: artifacts are addressed by it,
so a bake bundle from a different commit than the client expecting its output
produces artifacts nobody ever looks for — a failure that is otherwise silent.
It is read from the job worker bundle itself (jobs.worker), so it says what this
installation would actually run.

A running server reports the same build string at GET /v1/capabilities.
